title: Sizing the Risk: Kelly, VIX, and Hybrid Approaches in Put-Writing on Index Options

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper evaluates systematic short put-writing strategies on S&P 500 Index weekly options (SPXW) using three position sizing methods: the Kelly criterion (estimated via Monte Carlo simulations with historical volatility estimators like close-to-close, Garman-Klass, and Yang-Zhang), VIX-rank volatility regime scaling, and a hybrid approach combining both. Strategies are tested across a grid of days-to-expiration (0 to 5 DTE), moneyness levels (0% to 10% OTM), and estimator lookback windows. Performance is evaluated on out-of-sample data from 2024 and in-sample data from 2018-2023 against buy-and-hold and CBOE PutWrite index benchmarks.
extraction.universe: S&P 500 Index weekly options (SPXW) and underlying S&P 500 Index

performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The B&H benchmark achieved an annualized return of 24% with a volatility of 12.63%, resulting in an information ratio of 1.9, an exceptionally strong outcome.
The PUT index delivered 17.93% annualized returns with significantly lower volatility of 6.52%, producing an outstanding information ratio of 2.75.

performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The most aggressive configurations—5 DTE, at-the-money options, using VIX9D with a 21-day memory—achieved the highest return (52.77%) with 21.59% volatility and a maximum drawdown of 9.91%.

key_findings: Ultra-short-dated (0-1 DTE) and far out-of-the-money (5%-10% OTM) put options deliver superior risk-adjusted returns and information ratios.
The hybrid position sizing method, combining the Kelly criterion with VIX-based volatility regime scaling, effectively balances return generation with robust drawdown control.
Advanced volatility estimators such as Garman-Klass and Yang-Zhang outperform simple close-to-close historical volatility by incorporating intraday price action and opening jumps.
The 9-day VIX (VIX9D) generally outperforms the standard 30-day VIX as a conditioning signal for short-dated option strategies.
limitations: The study focuses exclusively on S&P 500 index options.
The out-of-sample period (2024) covers a strong bull market and does not encompass extreme market dislocations or alternative volatility regimes.
